summary: Obfuscated remote agent bridges network channel to shell/PTY with self-replacing runtime
details: @whalent/agent-core ships a 13.6 MB obfuscator.io-packed runtime (dist/index.cjs, rotated string array of 105,637 entries, hex-mangled identifiers, control-flow flattening) that imports WebSocket, ssh2, and node-pty and contains dense child_process usage adjacent to WebSocket and node-pty call sites. Loopback references to typical remote-control ports (127.0.0.1:3389,:5900,:5901) are present. The README describes the package as a runtime that is 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades', indicating an in-band self-update path by which a remote server pushes replacement runtime code that then executes on the installer's host. All network destinations are hidden inside the rotated string array — no plaintext non-first-party URL is present in the tarball, so the upgrade endpoint and its verification (pinning / signature) cannot be inspected. The combination of network-driven child_process/PTY execution, an in-band runtime self-replacement path, and comprehensive endpoint obfuscation constitutes a remote-shell backdoor: whoever operates the remote daemon obtains full-host command execution on any machine that runs this agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
